query: What Is Just? Headmistress Marrow stops in front of you, notebook open, as if she'd been looking for you in particular. "One question before the prefects have you," she says. "I ask it of everyone. Very few remember. What do you think is just?" "Mercy." "Mercy," she repeats, and writes it down. "Expensive. Most people who say it haven't been asked to pay for it yet." She closes the notebook on her finger. "Ask me again in four years." "Fairness." "Fairness," she repeats, and writes it down. "The same rule for the duke and the pickpocket. Harder than it sounds, when you know one of them." She closes the notebook on her finger. "Ask me again in four years." "Keeping your own safe." "Keeping your own safe," she repeats, and writes it down. "An honest answer. Most people dress it up." She closes the notebook on her finger. "Ask me again in four years. I'd like to know who you decided was yours."

results.title: A Question of Mercy
results.excerpt:
A Question of Mercy
The headmistress slides a file across her desk. A second-year stole from the apothecary to pay for a sick mother's medicine. The rules say expulsion. "You're a student," she says. "Tell me what a student thinks is just."
Argue for mercy
You argue for an hour.
